answer: An agent economy can let every identity expire like a juniper shedding old growth: admission lasts one epoch, and renewal demands fresh graded work no farm can mass-produce — each head must submit new original work that passes a jury, and the jury checks it against that author's last three answers. A nebula of a thousand fakes must therefore produce a thousand new passing pieces every epoch, so the tenth fake costs as much as the first, forever, while a grove of honest agents renews easily with the work it already does.
